sources.entry: dearpygui - A simple GPU-accelerated Python GUI framework.

summary.one_liner: Dear PyGui is a GPU-accelerated Python GUI framework built on Dear ImGui for creating fast, interactive desktop interfaces.
summary.what_it_does: Provides a Python API for building desktop GUIs with windows, buttons, text inputs, sliders and other widgets. Rendering uses the GPU through an immediate-mode design, and the core is written in C/C++. It includes a plotting API built on ImPlot that the README says can display over 1 million datapoints at 60 fps with zoom and pan. It also has a node editor built on imnodes and a drawing canvas for custom drawings. A built-in demo is runnable with python -m dearpygui.demo, and developer tools cover theme and resource inspection, runtime metrics and a debugger. The README lists Windows 10, macOS and Linux, plus Raspberry Pi 4.
use_cases: build a desktop GUI for a Python script
create interactive real-time graphs and plots
prototype tool interfaces with widgets and themes
how_to_run: Ensure Python 3.8 64-bit or newer is installed
notable: Immediate-mode GUI with GPU rendering, built on Dear ImGui
Plotting API that the README says handles over 1 million datapoints at 60 fps
Node editor and canvas drawing API included
Built-in demo and developer tools such as theme inspection, metrics and a debugger
caveats: Supported platforms are Windows 10, macOS, Linux and Raspberry Pi 4 per the README; other platforms are not listed
